minor.author: zdunekhere@gmail.com
minor.comment: First release of @livesession/libstylist, LiveSession's tooling for a self-describing DOM: every component root is a namespaced custom tag (<elo-alert>) or a value-less marker (<button elo-button>), and styling goes through hashed, value-less part attributes, never class. Ships the cx() runtime (cx, CxAttrs, cxData, hostProps, unsetRef, plus the legacy() / legacyClassName() helpers for a codebase mid-migration), the Babel and Vite plugins (required for inline cx() data literals — without them the data renders nothing and a dev warning fires; library builds bundle the runtime as virtual:libstylist/runtime), the PostCSS plugin and registry (part maps with $tags, stylist-registry.json, the lock projection), the ESLint rules and stylelint preset, libstylist check / burndown, gen-types, hash, the codemod from the cx attribute to cx() calls, and migrate-selectors, which rewrites a consumer app's ls-* selectors from @livesession/eloquentui-css/migration/ls-to-elo.json. The design-system packages bundle the runtime, so consumers install libstylist only to author their own cx() code or run the CLI.

minor.author: zdunekhere@gmail.com
minor.comment: feat(libstylist): directory namespaces — package.json `libstylist.namespaces` maps package-relative directories to a namespace of their own (`"src/render": "render"`, or `{ namespace, segment?, word? }`); a file takes the longest directory containing it, so an app's `RenderInvitationRow` in src/render is `<crm-render-invitationrow>`. `resolvePackageConfig` returns the file's effective config (plus its base config and directory) through a cached package finder (`findLibstylistPackage`) and a per-file pick (`packageConfigOf`); the transform, the lint rules (tag-name, rootLocals, segment discovery), gen-types and the checker follow it

minor.author: zdunekhere@gmail.com
minor.comment: feat(libstylist): a component declared in a package whose package.json has a libstylist prefix (the design system's dist, linked or installed) is a delegate to the checker, not a third-party component — an app component may root on `<Table crm-x {...cx(cn.root, rest)}>` without a wrapper (without the marker: R106; a marker forwarded onto one its declaration marks `@libstylistRoot none`, such as `Loader` or a provider, never reaches the DOM: R106 too); a `#` subpath import (`#components`) is the package's own module to the lint rules and the codemod, like a relative one

minor.author: zdunekhere@gmail.com
minor.comment: feat(libstylist): override sheets — an app restyles a design-system component everywhere with plain CSS: `@stylist override <Component | sheet-id> from "<package>" [within <AppComponent>];` then `.root` (the component's identity, `:is(tag,[tag])`, custom tag and marker alike) and its part names as classes, compiled by `stylistOverride()` (after postcss-nesting) into the overrides layer with a class's specificity; `collectOverrideSheet` (pass 1) and `resolveOverrides` (`/registry`: the package's prefix and namespace, the target sheet, parts and resets, `within` against the app registry, one sheet per design-system sheet) report `invalid-override`, `unresolved-package`, `unknown-target`, `unknown-part`, `unknown-within`, `duplicate-override`, `shared-reset`, `reset-within` and `keyframes-clash` with did-you-mean; `@stylist reset [<part> …];` strips the design system's own declarations of those parts from its stylesheets at build time (`resetCss`/`stylistReset()`: per rule subject, custom properties kept, selector lists split, `:is()` alternatives guarded with a zero-specificity `:where(:not())`, idempotent) with a report of what each reset drops and the layout declarations the override doesn't re-declare (`resetReports`, `formatResetReports`, `[empty-reset]`); the lock takes optional `overrides`/`resets` sections (`toLock(registry, overrideLock)`, `diffLock` kinds `override`/`reset`); `/workspace` adds `compileOverride`, `overridesLayerProblem` and `renderOverridesModule`; `@stylist override`/`reset` in a package sheet are errors; the workspace tooling applies them: `css.overrides` in libstylist.config.mjs (`dir`, `registries` — the design system's css packages, found installed —, `layer`, placed after `components` and before the namespace layers by the loader and the default order statement), override sheets never a package's sheets (an overrides directory inside a sheet directory is left out of its registry and part maps; `compileSheet` refuses them), `buildWorkspace` resolving them against the installed design systems (`collectOverrides`, `from` resolved to the component package installed where the sheet is; `design-system` and `overrides-index` errors), `libstylist build [--check|--watch]` compiling them, writing the generated overrides module and the lock's override sections, printing the reset report (a stale lock lists the entries that moved), `stylistWorkspace()` compiling override sheets into the overrides layer and stripping every stylesheet of the design system's css package of the resets as the app imports it (HMR: a changed reset set reloads the design-system stylesheets, a rebuilt design system the override sheets reading it; the report in the terminal, errors on the overlay; `vite build` fails on `[empty-reset]`, `[unbundled-reset]`, `[overrides-not-imported]` and a stale overrides module; `overrides: false` opts a build out), `libstylist check` rule S310, and the stylelint preset reading override sheets (`directive-syntax`: the override grammar and placement; `sheet-root`: `.root` is the identity, document context before it); override hardening: a reset part styled only through shared `:is()` rules is reset by its guards and counted (no false `[empty-reset]`/`[unbundled-reset]`; `touchedTargets` replaces `droppedTargets`), a guarded rule keeps its custom properties for the reset element, a statement a strip leaves last is ended with `;` (a bundler's concatenation no longer swallows the next stylesheet), layout notes cover zero minima, relative sizes and auto margins and are acknowledged only by a re-declaration under the same conditions (`acknowledgedDeclarations`/`acknowledges` replace `acknowledgedProperties`), an override rule's subject must be `.root`, a part or inside one (`:has()`, `+`, `~` no longer escape the component), `:component()` of the same design system is allowed as context (resolved, locked; `[unresolved-ref]`), a sheet id must be kebab-case (`[invalid-override]` at resolution), `@stylist override Tooltip` points at the `tooltip` sheet, a declaration a design-system `!important` beats is an `[important]` warning (`importantDeclarations`, `importantConflicts`, `designSystemImportants`, `importantWarnings`), `vite build` fails on `[layer-order]` (`declaredLayerOrder`, `bundleLayerProblem`), `vite build --watch` re-reads override sheets and re-transforms them and the design system's stylesheets on every rebuild, and dev HMR looks modules up by posix path

minor.author: zdunekhere@gmail.com
minor.comment: feat(libstylist): packages whose sources are not `src`, and the aliases they import each other by — `sources` on a config package (and in a package.json `libstylist` field, which `workspacePackages()` passes on and a config value must equal; default `["src"]`; package-relative, existing, never nested) is what `gen-types` scans for custom tags (with `--config`, or from the package.json field; the generated header names the directories) and what `stylistWorkspace()`'s JSX transform owns (`workspaceSourcePattern`); a top-level `typescript: { paths }` (tsconfig `paths` semantics, targets relative to the config file) joins the package-name paths in the TypeScript program of `check` and the codemod, so a component imported as `~/pages/settings/…` is no longer `any` (no false R105/T203). Malformed values are config errors; a config without either behaves exactly as before.

minor.author: zdunekhere@gmail.com
minor.comment: feat(libstylist): packages sharing namespaces — the checker config takes `packages[].namespaces` (equal to package.json's) and `packages[].sheets` (the package's own sheet directories, one css group per namespace: `crm-accounts`, `crm-accounts.render`) instead of a cssGroup, `css.dir` only when a package has a cssGroup, and one naming per namespace instead of one package per namespace; components are named from their implementation file, tags and scopes stay unique across packages (T201 names both packages), S302 checks the sheet's package and namespace and burndown counts per package. `partMapGroups` resolves a specifier serving several groups (a package's `#css`); `@livesession/libstylist/workspace` exports the sheet grouping

minor.author: zdunekhere@gmail.com
minor.comment: runtime: withoutStylist(props) — props without the part attributes and markers cx(props) forwards, for a component whose root takes them while its other props spread onto an inner element (TextInput's native input). Moved from the React package and infinity, which each kept a copy; SPEC §6 and AUTHORING document it.

minor.author: zdunekhere@gmail.com
minor.comment: feat(libstylist): the workspace build for app packages that keep their sheets next to their sources — `libstylist build [--config] [--check] [--watch]` writes each package's generated `#css` part-map module (side-effect sheet imports, one `as const` map per sheet; `no-hash-literal` skips it), the committed lock (`css.lock`; compared as data and written with the indentation on disk, so a formatter's rewrite is no drift) and the gitignored registry (`css.registry`, which the checker, the codemod and a config loaded with `loadCheckConfig` default to the build's output when no package has a cssGroup; S309 then says to run `libstylist build`), failing on registry errors and on export names shared within one module or specifier; `stylistWorkspace()` from `@livesession/libstylist/vite` runs the transform over the workspace packages' sources and compiles their sheets at import time into cascade layers (`css.layers`), rewriting part maps in dev (catching up on every package once a registry error is fixed) and failing `vite build` on stale ones; `@livesession/libstylist/workspace` adds `workspacePackages`/`partMapsFor` (config packages discovered from pnpm-workspace.yaml), `buildWorkspace`, `compileSheet`, `renderPartMapModule` and `runWorkspaceBuild`; `gen-types --config` covers every package of a config; `packages[].sheets` may be `[]`; postcss-nesting is an optional peer

patch.author: zdunekhere@gmail.com
patch.comment: Declare @typescript-eslint/utils as a dependency: the ./eslint entry imports it at runtime, so it failed to load in a consumer that installs only @typescript-eslint/parser (or installs typescript-eslint without hoisting). @types/react is now an optional peer for the ./jsx typings.

patch.author: zdunekhere@gmail.com
patch.comment: The libstylist bin is a committed launcher (bin/libstylist.mjs) that loads the built CLI, so it is linked even when the workspace is installed before it is built.
